components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single routine primary action in a view.
components.css: .ds-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; height:36px; padding:0 16px; border-radius:10px; font:500 14px/1 Inter, sans-serif; border:none; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary { background:var(--primary, oklch(0.58 0.172 36.44)); color:#fff; box-shadow:0px 1px 3px 0px hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.10), 0px 1px 2px -1px hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.10); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, oklch(0.58 0.172 36.44)), black 12%); } .ds-btn:active { translate:0 1px; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.58 0.172 36.44)); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; height:36px; padding:0 16px; border-radius:10px; border:none; font:500 14px/1 Inter, sans-serif; background:var(--destructive, oklch(0.6368 0.2078 25.33)); color:#fff; box-shadow:0px 1px 3px 0px hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.10), 0px 1px 2px -1px hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.10); cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive, oklch(0.6368 0.2078 25.33)), black 10%); } .ds-btn-danger:active { translate:0 1px; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.58 0.172 36.44)); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; height:36px; padding:0 16px; border-radius:10px; font:500 14px/1 Inter, sans-serif; background:var(--card, #fff); color:var(--foreground, oklch(0.3211 0 0)); border:1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.9022 0.0052 247.88)); cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background:var(--secondary, oklch(0.967 0.0029 264.54)); } .ds-btn-outline:active { translate:0 1px; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.58 0.172 36.44)); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.css: .ds-input { height:36px; width:260px; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:10px; border:1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.9022 0.0052 247.88)); background:var(--card, #fff); color:var(--foreground, oklch(0.3211 0 0)); font:400 14px/1.5 Inter, sans-serif; transition:border-color 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color:var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.551 0.0234 264.36)); } .ds-input:hover { border-color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--border, oklch(0.9022 0.0052 247.88)), var(--foreground, oklch(0.3211 0 0)) 18%); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.58 0.172 36.44)); outline-offset:2px; border-color:transparent; }

components.name: Badges

components.name: Seal Confirm
components.description: Type-to-arm, press-and-hold ceremony for irreversible writes.
components.css: .ds-seal-wrap { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px; width:360px; font-family:Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-seal-label { font-size:14px; font-weight:500; color:var(--foreground, oklch(0.3211 0 0)); } .ds-seal-label code { font:12px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; padding:2px 6px; border-radius:4px; background:var(--muted, oklch(0.9846 0.0017 247.84)); } .ds-seal { position:relative; height:44px; width:100%; overflow:hidden; border-radius:10px; border:1px solid var(--destructive, oklch(0.6368 0.2078 25.33)); background:transparent; cursor:pointer; } .ds-seal-ink { position:absolute; inset:0; transform-origin:left; transform:scaleX(0); background:var(--destructive, oklch(0.6368 0.2078 25.33)); transition:transform 140ms ease-out; } .ds-seal:active .ds-seal-ink { transform:scaleX(1); transition:transform 700ms linear; } .ds-seal-face { position:relative; font-size:14px; font-weight:500; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.12em; color:var(--destructive, oklch(0.6368 0.2078 25.33)); } .ds-seal:active .ds-seal-face { color:#fff; } .ds-seal:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.58 0.172 36.44)); outline-offset:2px; }

narrative.overview:
God Mode is a control room for the live Carmen database. The operator always knows which system they are connected to, reads dense data quickly, and acts through controls that have weight. Most of the room is calm and familiar. Its cool-gray surfaces, Inter type, sidebar rail and zebra tables come from carmen-backstage, so someone who works in both tools feels at home. The deviations exist only where a mistake would be permanent.

Two places deliberately break that family resemblance. One is the live-target bar, a strip pinned above every page that names the target database and turns alarm-red whenever the target is not local. The other is the confirm ceremony: you type a phrase to arm the control, then press and hold to fire it. All of the system's distinctiveness goes into these two elements and nowhere else. The terracotta primary carries routine action. Red is reserved for danger and never decorates.

Interactions are tactile and deliberate. Buttons drop 1px when pressed. The seal control fills with ink from left to right while held. Pages settle in with a 4px rise. Motion always reports state and is never ornament, and all of it respects prefers-reduced-motion. The layout targets desktop only; the mobile drawer exists as a fallback and is not a designed experience.
keyCharacteristics: Cool-gray canvas, white working surfaces and hairline borders, with near-flat depth.
One warm accent (Fired Terracotta) for routine action. Red means only "this is dangerous".
Dense, scannable data: 14px body, 12px uppercase column heads, and JetBrains Mono for IDs, hosts, timestamps and SQL.
The live-target bar is always visible. The confirm ceremony protects every irreversible write.
Light and dark themes are both first-class, switched by a .dark class on <html>.

rules.name: The Red Means Danger Rule
rules.body: Alarm red appears only where a write is irreversible or the target is live. It is never used for emphasis, branding or decoration.

rules.name: The One Warm Voice Rule
rules.body: Fired Terracotta is the only saturated hue in routine UI. Each view gets one primary button. Everything else is outline or ghost.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every status pairs its colour with an icon and words. The target bar has a triangle icon plus "Every write is permanent", and each alert has its own lucide icon.

rules.name: The Mono Is Literal Rule
rules.body: Mono type is used only for values the system reads exactly (identifiers, phrases to type, SQL). It is never used for emphasis.

rules.name: The Border Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: A new container separates itself with a Hairline border and a surface tone, never with a shadow.

dos: Do consume god-mode token names (bg-surface, text-foreground-muted, bg-accent, bg-danger). Re-skinning happens in the adapter layer of app/globals.css, not in components.
Do route every irreversible write through the Seal Confirm ceremony, with a blast-radius preview before it.
Do keep the live-target bar on every authenticated page.
Do set identifiers, hosts, SQL and confirm phrases in JetBrains Mono.
Do check both light and dark themes. Every new token needs a .dark value or must derive through var() / color-mix().
Do keep motion functional: the 1px press, the 220ms page-in, the 150ms row hover, the 700ms hold fill. All of it is gated by prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use alarm red or the danger fill for anything that isn't destructive or live.
Don't add a second loud, god-mode-specific element. The target bar and the confirm ceremony are the only places where the system departs from carmen-backstage.
Don't convey status by colour alone. Pair it with an icon and text.
Don't add shadows to cards or containers. Use a Hairline border and surface tone.
Don't reintroduce the retired Ledger identity (aged paper, serif display, wax seal).
